geometry_used.excavation_plan_ASSUMPTION: footprint plus working/retention zone, say 36 x 30 m or larger; site boundary UNKNOWN

desk_study_before_drilling: geology and hydrogeology maps, previous investigations on or near the site (verify availability)
historic land use and contamination screening; made ground, fill, landfill, mining, karst, voids
flood maps, river/sea level, tidal influence on groundwater

boreholes.location: within the 12 x 8 m core, near centre
boreholes.depth_rule: deepest hole: the greater of (a) about 1.5 to 2 x the raft/group width B (B = 24 m) below founding level or to the depth where net stress increase falls to an engineer-set fraction of in-situ stress, and (b) pile toe depth plus an engineer-set depth (often several pile diameters, or 1.5 x group width, below toe) ; if rock is met, an engineer-set socket depth in rock (verify code)
boreholes.purpose: profile under the highest load; settlement and pile design; sampling for lab tests
boreholes.numeric_depth_m: UNKNOWN until pile/raft option and ground are known; indicative planning range 40 to 60 m is a budgeting placeholder only (JUDGMENT)

boreholes.location: four corners of the tower footprint, positioned just outside or at the edge so as not to be lost in the pile/raft layout, inside the excavation line
boreholes.depth_rule: at least the deeper of (a) founding level + 1.0 to 1.5 x B and (b) the retention wall toe + engineer-set depth (below the deepest of any hydraulic cut-off / heave check depth); at least two of the four to the full depth of BH-C
boreholes.purpose: variability across the footprint, differential settlement, tilt risk, retaining wall design

boreholes.location: on the excavation perimeter / retaining wall line, at least one on each long side, near the most sensitive neighbour
boreholes.depth_rule: retention wall toe depth plus engineer-set margin; deeper if a low-permeability layer is needed as a cut-off

boreholes.location: added wherever the first holes disagree (changing stratigraphy, dipping rock, soft pockets, fill)
boreholes.purpose: target: no unexplained variation between points; spacing to be reduced where ground is variable

total_boreholes_proposed: 7 minimum (1 core + 4 corners + 2 perimeter), plus contingency holes (JUDGMENT; verify minimum number/spacing against the local code and EN 1997-2 or equivalent)

cpts.location: paired close (about 2 to 5 m, not in the same hole) to each borehole and additional points on a grid across the footprint, including the core centre
cpts.depth_rule: to refusal or the borehole depth, whichever is shallower; if refusal occurs in a possibly non-bearing layer (cobbles, dense lens) it is verified by the adjacent borehole
cpts.purpose: continuous profile, layering, pore pressure, liquefaction screening, correlation with SPT/lab; includes pore-pressure dissipation tests at selected depths for groundwater and consolidation parameters

in_situ_tests.test: SPT (energy-measured, with sampler type and rod length recorded)
in_situ_tests.where: in all boreholes, typically at 1.5 m intervals and at stratum changes in granular or mixed soils
in_situ_tests.why: index of density and correlation; liquefaction screening; correlation to CPT

in_situ_tests.test: Undisturbed sampling (thin-wall piston / Shelby, block, triple-tube core barrel)

in_situ_tests.where: at least in BH-C and one corner, in the stratum proposed for founding or pile bearing, and in weak rock / very dense or stiff layers where SPT and CPT are poor
in_situ_tests.why: stiffness at working strain for settlement of the raft and pile group; limit pressure for design checks
permeability of rock for dewatering and cut-off

in_situ_tests.where: aquifer layers affecting the basement, at least one full-scale pumping test with observation wells where dewatering is expected to be significant
in_situ_tests.why: permeability and storage for dewatering design and neighbour drawdown

in_situ_tests.test: Pile load test (preliminary, instrumented) - NOT part of site investigation but flagged
in_situ_tests.where: once a pile option is chosen, before detailed design
in_situ_tests.why: calibrates pile capacity and stiffness; programme and cost item

in_situ_tests.test: Geophysics (MASW / downhole / crosshole / cross-hole or suspension logging) for shear-wave velocity
in_situ_tests.where: downhole in BH-C and one corner (or the SCPTu), MASW across the site as check
in_situ_tests.why: Vs profile to the depth required by the seismic code to classify the site class (commonly top 30 m but deeper where required, verify), and for soil-structure interaction and site response; deeper profiling to bedrock may be needed if a site-specific response analysis is required (verify)

in_situ_tests.test: Cross-hole or downhole to bedrock / site-specific ground-response data
in_situ_tests.where: decided after seismic hazard and local code known
in_situ_tests.why: site-specific response analysis if the code requires it for tall buildings or soft soils (verify)

groundwater_monitoring.installations: standpipe or vibrating-wire piezometers in each distinct aquifer and perched layer (at least 3 to 4 locations on the site, with response zones in different strata), plus a deep one below the basement base
groundwater_monitoring.duration: minimum several months, ideally one full hydrological year to capture seasonal high and low (verify requirement); with readings at least monthly and data loggers at selected points; add tidal/river correlation if applicable
groundwater_monitoring.why: design uplift (flotation) uses the maximum credible groundwater level, which may be much higher than the level measured in a single drilling campaign; dewatering uses the range and the hydraulic gradient; the design level is set by the engineer (and local code) not by this scope
groundwater_monitoring.also: record artesian pressure, water chemistry, and neighbouring wells / pumping; include the hydraulic conductivity from pumping and falling-head tests

laboratory_tests: classification: moisture content, Atterberg limits, particle size distribution (sieve + hydrometer), particle density, organic content

strength: unconsolidated undrained and consolidated (isotropically or anisotropically) triaxial with pore pressure measurement, direct shear / ring shear where residual strength matters, UCS for cohesive and weak rock
stiffness and compressibility: oedometer (including unload-reload and creep/secondary compression), small-strain stiffness via bender elements or local strain measurement for deep excavations

dynamic / cyclic: cyclic simple shear or cyclic triaxial on undisturbed or reconstituted samples of potentially liquefiable layers, resonant column for G-gamma curves where site response is required (verify)
rock: UCS, point load, Brazilian, density, slake durability, RQD from cores, joint characterization, rock-socket interface where used
swelling / collapse / dispersivity where relevant to the soil type found
permeability: constant/falling head in lab (supplement to field tests)

chemical (aggressivity): pH, sulphate (water and soil-extract), chloride, magnesium, ammonium, aggressive CO2, resistivity, organic content, to classify exposure of concrete and steel (limits from the local code or standard, verify)

contamination: screening and laboratory analysis for metals, hydrocarbons, PAHs, asbestos, ground gas (methane, CO2) and groundwater contaminants, with the suite set by the environmental regulator (verify); informs disposal of excavated material and dewatering discharge
rock_coring_if_rock_met: Core with triple-tube barrel at least to an engineer-set depth into rock (commonly several metres or more than a pile-diameter multiple; verify), log RQD, fracture spacing and weathering grade, check for solution cavities / voids beyond the borehole (probing or geophysics for karst), packer tests, UCS tests and, if rock sockets are intended, rock-mass quality along the socket length.

decision_rules.pushed_toward_by: founding stratum within and below the excavation is laterally consistent across BH-C and BH-1..4 and is of a stiffness the settlement analysis shows can carry the factored/service tower load with total and differential settlements and tilt below limits to be set by the structural engineer; no compressible, loose, organic or collapsible layer within the stress influence depth (about 1.5 to 2 x B); groundwater not causing unmanageable uplift; liquefaction not predicted
decision_rules.pushed_away_by: any of the above not satisfied
decision_rules.data_that_decides: CPT/SPT/PMT stiffness profile, oedometer data, variation between holes, settlement analysis (limits to be set by engineer)

decision_rules.pushed_toward_by: shallow ground is soft, loose, organic, fill, liquefiable or highly variable, or a competent stratum (dense granular, hard clay or rock) exists at a depth that a pile can reach and be proved; ground conditions allow the chosen installation method (noise, vibration and neighbour limits); the raft alone would exceed settlement or tilt limits
decision_rules.pushed_away_by: no competent stratum within a reachable depth; obstructions; artesian pressure; karst; neighbouring structures that cannot tolerate installation effects
decision_rules.data_that_decides: depth and continuity of the bearing stratum, rock level and quality, negative skin friction potential (compressible layer plus fill), lateral loads from seismic action, pile load test results

decision_rules.pushed_toward_by: raft alone satisfies bearing capacity (to be shown) but settlement or differential settlement exceeds limits, and the ground beneath the raft is reasonably uniform and not liquefiable; piles used as settlement reducers with the raft carrying part of the load
decision_rules.pushed_away_by: liquefiable layers, soft deep layers that cause continued consolidation settlement, uncertain raft-soil contact (voids, softening), absence of reliable data for the raft-soil interaction
decision_rules.data_that_decides: load-settlement response from preliminary pile tests, soil stiffness from small-strain data, consolidation behaviour, and a 3D soil-structure interaction analysis (code treatment of piled rafts: verify)

decision_rules.option: ground improvement (densification, stone columns, deep soil mixing, grouting, preloading with drains)
decision_rules.pushed_toward_by: problem layer is limited in thickness and extent (for example a liquefiable layer, soft clay or loose fill) and a competent layer lies beneath; improvement is feasible and verifiable (pre/post CPT) and acceptable to neighbours (vibration, spoil, groundwater)
decision_rules.pushed_away_by: problem extends to depth beyond practical improvement; contamination mobilised by treatment; fine-grained soils where densification is ineffective; no time for preloading
decision_rules.data_that_decides: CPT-based layer thickness and fines content, cyclic test results, depth to competent layer, trial area results

decision_rules.pushed_toward_by: loose to medium saturated sand/silt layers (CPT/SPT/Vs + fines content + groundwater depth) and a seismic hazard that is not low; the hazard level comes from the jurisdiction's maps (UNKNOWN)
decision_rules.outcome: if susceptible: piles through the layer designed for loss of support and lateral spreading, ground improvement, or relocation; screening method and acceptance factor are set by the local code (verify)

options: secant or contiguous bored pile wall
sheet pile (limited depth, vibration, water-tight if interlocked)
soil nailing (needs space and no neighbouring underground structures, above the water table or with dewatering)
top-down construction with permanent floors as props
anchors (need neighbour consent for tendons beyond boundary) or internal struts
basement_excavation_risks.data_that_decides: soil strength and stiffness, groundwater level and permeability, depth to rock or hydraulic cut-off layer, neighbour distance and sensitivity, available site width, noise/vibration limits, utilities, construction programme

basement_excavation_risks.mechanism: pumping lowers groundwater, increasing effective stress in compressible layers outside the excavation and causing settlement; also may mobilise contamination, wash out fines
basement_excavation_risks.data_that_decides: permeability, aquifer thickness and boundaries, recharge, compressible layer thickness and its stress history, contamination plume, the discharge consent
basement_excavation_risks.mitigation_options: cut-off wall embedded in a low-permeability stratum, recharge wells, staged excavation, reducing drawdown inside the box, monitoring wells, settlement monitoring

basement_excavation_risks.risk: effects on neighbouring buildings, roads and utilities
basement_excavation_risks.mechanism: wall deflection, ground loss, dewatering drawdown, vibration from installation
basement_excavation_risks.data_that_decides: condition survey of neighbours (including foundations), small-strain soil stiffness, wall stiffness, numerical prediction of movement, trigger levels set with the neighbours' owners and the authority
basement_excavation_risks.mitigation_options: stiffer wall, top-down sequence, more props, underpinning, protective monitoring with action levels

basement_excavation_risks.mechanism: undrained shear failure of soft clay below the excavation, or hydraulic uplift/piping where a low-permeability layer overlies a pressurised aquifer, or excess unloading heave
basement_excavation_risks.data_that_decides: undrained shear strength profile, depth of the stiff layer below the base, piezometric pressure in layers beneath the base, thickness of the layer between the base and aquifer, unload-reload stiffness
basement_excavation_risks.mitigation_options: deeper wall embedment, base slab by jet grouting, deep wells to relieve pressure, staged excavation

basement_excavation_risks.risk: uplift and flotation of the completed basement
basement_excavation_risks.mechanism: water pressure at the base exceeds the weight of structure available to resist it, especially when the tower is not yet complete (construction stage) or when the design groundwater level rises
basement_excavation_risks.data_that_decides: design maximum groundwater level and flood level (from monitoring and flood data, set by the engineer), basement geometry, weight at each construction stage, tension pile / anchor capacity if used (to be derived, not assumed)
basement_excavation_risks.mitigation_options: tension piles or anchors, extra ballast, permanent drainage (needs reliable maintenance and consent), staged dewatering until the weight is sufficient

basement_excavation_risks.mechanism: props, anchors, groundwater inflow, surcharge from cranes or stockpiles, wall toe stability, construction sequence
basement_excavation_risks.data_that_decides: full ground model, contractor method, monitoring data; design by a temporary works engineer with checking (jurisdiction-specific requirement, verify)
water level range, chemical aggressivity tests, chlorides, sulphates
